newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba slams Chilean Communist leader's arrest.
newsitem.headline: Cuba slams Chilean Communist leader's arrest.

text.p: Cuba, the only Communist nation in Latin America, Thursday strongly criticised the arrest of Chile's Communist Party leader, Gladys Marin.
The Cuban Communist Party published a statement in its daily newspaper, Granma, saying it hoped Marin would be free by the time Chile hosts an Ibero-American summit Nov. 9-11.
Marin was arrested this week after allegedly slandering former military ruler Augusto Pinochet.
The Cuban statement said Marin was an honest politician who had helped Chile's process of democratic opening and contributed to stabilising the country.

It said her arrest had provoked indignation around the world, and "it is hard to understand how this (arrest) is possible in a country struggling hard to consolidate peace, the rule of law and respect for citizens' rights."
"Our party is fully in solidarity with those around the world who call for the release of Gladys Marin, a worthy friend who was also always in solidarity with Cuba," the statement added.
Cuban President Fidel Castro is likely to attend the Ibero-American summit. But no announcement has been made that he will attend -- as usual with his travels.
Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said in Santiago Wednesday that Marin's arrest was likely to tarnish Chile's reputation abroad.

Police arrested Marin on a judge's orders, on charges she slandered Pinochet by calling him a psychopath and a blackmailer at a memorial service for the 3,200 people, including Marin's husband, killed during Pinochet's rule.
Pinochet, who toppled Marxist leader Salvador Allende in a 1973 coup, ceded the presidency to civilians in 1990 but remains the commander-in-chief of the armed forces.
